findings.title: Hotkey settings restart stops a non-existent manager

evidence.detail: rg '_ghk|global_hotkeys' shows dialogs.py is the only _ghk reference; the real manager is runtime_services.global_hotkeys.
AppRuntimeServices.init_global_hotkeys assigns self.global_hotkeys = None before creating a new manager and does not stop the old manager first.

        config["text_scale"] = new_text_scale

        config["hud_enabled"] = new_hud_enabled

findings.title: Win32 window style setup reports success on API failure
findings.impact: On Windows, failed SetWindowLongW or SetLayeredWindowAttributes calls can leave the main/HUD window non-transparent or non-click-through while callers proceed as if lock/click-through succeeded.
findings.fix: Declare ctypes argtypes/restype with wintypes, check BOOL/last-error return values, and return False when any required style or layered attribute call fails.

evidence.detail: ctypes Win32 BOOL failures do not raise OSError by default; this code ignores both SetWindowLongW and SetLayeredWindowAttributes return values and returns True.
tests/test_system_portability.py only covers non-Windows user32 absence, not Windows API failure returns.

findings.title: HUD can fall back to a non-click-through topmost window
findings.impact: If Win32 layered setup fails while Tk color-key support exists, click_through=True falls back to only setting Tk alpha, leaving a topmost HUD that can intercept game clicks.
findings.fix: When click_through is requested and Win32.setup_window fails, raise HUDOverlayUnavailable or hide/destroy HUD; reserve Tk-only fallback for non-click-through contexts.

evidence.detail: Fallback path applies only window.attributes("-alpha") and has no click-through equivalent.
tests/test_hud_overlay.py raises only when tk_color_key=False; it does not cover the tk_color_key=True click-through failure path.

findings.title: Showing primary reticle re-shows stale secondary markers
findings.impact: When secondary targets drop from a previous frame, _render_secondary_targets hides unused IDs, then _set_reticle_visible(True) marks every secondary item normal again, potentially showing stale or empty secondary markers.
findings.fix: Let _render_secondary_targets own secondary visibility; _set_reticle_visible should hide secondary IDs only when visible is false or split primary and secondary visibility.

evidence.detail: _render_reticle calls _render_secondary_targets at hud_overlay.py:999-1007 and then _set_reticle_visible(True) at line 1012.
_render_secondary_targets hides unused/empty secondary IDs at hud_overlay.py:878-884.

findings.title: GlobalHotkeys.stop can miss startup race
findings.impact: If stop runs immediately after start before _run stores _tid, it returns without setting _stop_event or joining, allowing the worker to proceed into GetMessageW and keep hotkeys registered until process exit.
findings.fix: Always set _stop_event and join an existing worker; coordinate readiness with an Event and check PostThreadMessageW success.

evidence.detail: start launches _run asynchronously at system.py:569-571; _tid is assigned inside _run at lines 589-592.
stop exits early solely because _tid is false at system.py:575-576.

findings.title: Custom non-WAV playback cannot be cancelled during shutdown
findings.impact: A long .mp3/.wma/.mid custom alert blocks the worker in MCI "play ... wait"; stop(drain=False) only discards queued jobs and joins with a timeout, so active playback can outlive shutdown.
findings.fix: Track the active MCI alias and use non-blocking playback with explicit stop/close from SoundManager.stop, or enforce a short custom alert duration.

evidence.detail: SoundManager.stop(drain=False) discards pending jobs and joins with timeout but has no path to interrupt active MCI wait.
_play_audio_file_mci uses blocking "play alias wait" for non-WAV custom files.

findings.title: NavigationWindow Win32 handle lookup can crash before fallback
findings.impact: On non-Windows or ctypes-limited environments, constructing NavigationWindow can raise at ctypes.windll.user32.GetParent before apply_window_styles reaches its guarded fallback.
findings.fix: Wrap handle acquisition in _WIN32_ACCESS_ERRORS and fall back to int(internal_id), then let apply_window_styles degrade.

evidence.detail: apply_window_styles has a guarded fallback, but this unguarded handle acquisition runs first.
The main app has a similar Windows-only handle acquisition pattern; project primary target is Windows, so severity is low.

findings.title: Standalone toggle during history mode can lose restore intent
findings.impact: If a standalone nav window becomes visible while history mode is already active, suspend_for_history_mode(state_changed=False) hides it without recording restore intent, so leaving history mode can keep it hidden despite standalone mode.
findings.fix: When hiding a visible window during active history layout, record restore intent, or defer showing/toggling standalone mode until history mode exits.

evidence.detail: restore_after_history_mode only shows the window when _history_mode_window_was_visible is true.
suspend_for_history_mode only updates that flag on state_changed=True.

findings.title: Non-dict panels value crashes config migration
findings.impact: A valid JSON config such as {"config_version":1,"panels":null} crashes ConfigManager.load during migration instead of falling back, so startup or settings load can fail until the user manually edits or deletes the config.
findings.fix: Normalize nested sections before migration, e.g. treat non-dict panels as {}, and catch TypeError from migration in the tolerant load path.

evidence.detail: Probe ConfigManager._migrate_config({"config_version":1,"panels":None}) raised TypeError; list panels raised TypeError list indices must be integers or slices.
ConfigManager.load catches json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError, and OSError, but not TypeError from _migrate_config.

findings.title: Auto-update artifacts are hash-checked but not publisher-signed
findings.impact: A compromised update host or release account can publish a malicious ZIP/EXE plus matching SHA256; the launcher uses SHA256 as integrity but has no independent publisher authenticity check.
findings.fix: Add an offline signature over the manifest or artifact, pin the public key in the launcher, and verify signatures before download/install.

evidence.detail: Build manifest records package_sha256 but no signature field.
Reviewed launcher/update files use sha256 checks but no signature verification path.

findings.title: Launcher self-update does not rehash staged EXE at apply time
findings.impact: After download hash passes, a same-user process could replace the staged file while the detached PowerShell script waits for the launcher to exit; the modified EXE is then copied to the real launcher path.
findings.fix: Pass expected SHA256 into _stage_launcher_self_update and have the PowerShell script hash $staged immediately before Copy-Item and $replacement before Move-Item.

evidence.detail: Download hash check occurs before staging at launcher.pyw:1913-1920.
_stage_launcher_self_update is called without the expected hash at launcher.pyw:1929-1934, and the script waits up to 120 seconds before copying.

findings.title: Python repr is used as remote shell quoting
findings.impact: A CLI value containing shell substitution syntax can be expanded by the remote shell before python3 starts because repr may choose double quotes for the env assignment.
findings.fix: Use shlex.quote for every remote shell value or pass a JSON blob/stdin protocol instead of shell-interpreted env prefixes.

evidence.detail: repr("x'$(touch /tmp/pwn)") uses double quotes; POSIX shells expand $() inside double quotes in an env assignment.
deploy_update_assets.py constructs one shell string passed to ssh as the remote command.

findings.title: Rollback can fail after changing app state and deleting preserved current version
findings.impact: If the final move from swap_dir to previous_dir fails after the first two moves, app_dir already contains the previous version, the function raises, and finally deletes work_dir containing the old current version.
findings.fix: Track move phases and reverse the second move on failure, or preserve swap_dir outside work_dir until current_version is safely restored or stored.

evidence.detail: The except path only restores swap_dir when app_dir is missing; it does not handle failure after previous_dir was moved into app_dir.

findings.title: Version comparison treats prerelease digits as newer stable versions
findings.impact: A remote version like 2.0.0-rc.1 compares greater than local 2.0.0, and min_launcher_version 2.0.0-rc.1 can make stable 2.0.0 appear too old.
findings.fix: Use a SemVer or PEP 440 parser and explicitly reject or handle prerelease/build metadata; skip draft/prerelease GitHub releases unless opted in.

evidence.detail: extract_version_tuple("2.0.0-rc.1") yields (2,0,0,1), which compares newer than (2,0,0).
tests/test_launcher_core.py only covers numeric versions.

findings.title: Legacy build ignores version-info generation failure
findings.impact: If create_version_info.py fails, the batch script continues building without version metadata, or with a stale file_version_info.txt if one exists.
findings.fix: Delete file_version_info.txt before generation and fail immediately when create_version_info.py returns nonzero; optionally assert the generated file matches source metadata.

evidence.detail: The script checks only whether file_version_info.txt exists, not %ERRORLEVEL% from create_version_info.py.
The primary portable build path is tools/build_portable.py, so this affects the legacy script path.
